what: The areas of the balancing authorities the network page draws, DERIVED by the ERW from counties: each county is given to one balancing authority from the utilities that serve it. Not a published boundary. Reference geometry, not a table.

provenance.label: Derived map: each county is given to one balancing authority from the utilities that serve it (EIA-861). It is not a boundary any balancing authority or agency published.
provenance.publisher: U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA); county shapes: U.S. Census Bureau
provenance.title: Annual Electric Power Industry Report, Form EIA-861 detailed data files, 2025 (Service_Territory, Sales_Ult_Cust, Delivery_Companies, Short_Form)
provenance.license_quoted: U.S. government publications are in the public domain and are not subject to copyright protection. You may use and/or distribute any of our data, files, databases, reports, graphs, charts, and other information products that are on our website

county_shapes.origin: the U.S. Census Bureau's cartographic boundary files, 2017 edition, as TopoJSON (the us-atlas package the site already uses; no request)

provenance.rule: A utility's customers in a state under each of its balancing authority codes (Parts A, C and D of Sales_Ult_Cust, the delivery companies' file and the short form) are split evenly over the counties Service_Territory lists for it in that state. A county is given to the code with the most customers so allotted; where no utility of a county reports a customer, to the code most of its utilities name; a tie is no assignment. A balancing authority's area is the counties given to it, joined. A code that is not one of the page's grids is not drawn.

simplification.method: each balancing authority's counties joined (shapely unary_union), then Douglas-Peucker with topology kept (shapely simplify, preserve_topology)
simplification.note: each area is simplified on its own, so two neighbours' shared border may open or overlap by up to the tolerance

order: largest area first; the page draws in this order. No two areas overlap: a county has one balancing authority here
